page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by AWS Graviton arm64 processors operating at 3.3 GHz. The hardware layout supplies 192 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, eliminating resource contention associated with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 1536.0 GB, which scales to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

Storage and connectivity specifications include 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance store capacity and a baseline networking throughput of 100 Gbps. The instance does not feature dedicated graphics processing units (GPUs).

The 64-bit Arm architecture yields high physical core density and power efficiency relative to legacy x86 server classes, making large-scale parallel processing more compute-efficient. A primary architectural tradeoff involves the ephemeral behavior of the local NVMe storage, which necessitates network-based replication or persistent block volume integration to prevent data loss across instance stops.

Workload applicability centers on memory-bound and storage-demanding applications requiring heavy parallel compute. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as Redis, distributed caches, data warehousing platforms, high-volume ETL processing, and low-latency transactional databases relying on substantial local disk caches.
description: Amazon Web Services r9gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by 192 dedicated arm64 AWS Graviton processor cores running at 3.3 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading, each core provides an independent execution context paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, totaling 1536.0 GB of RAM. The server includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline networking throughput of 100 Gbps, with zero GPUs present. Its arm64 architecture delivers dense compute and power efficiency for high-scale parallel operations, balancing extensive memory footprint with fast local I/O. Given the ephemeral nature of local instance store disks, durable data architectures require independent persistence. The r9gd.48xlarge is tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, real-time big data analytics, distributed caches, and data warehousing tasks needing extreme memory and fast disk staging.
